name: Oasis
label: Creation Records
lede: A Burnage band that had to blag its way onto a Glasgow bill ended up as the biggest thing Creation Records ever had, sold out Knebworth twice over, split in a Paris dressing-room fight, and came back sixteen years later to stadiums full of people who weren't born the first time.

eras.title: The roadie's terms
eras.text: The band was Bonehead's, Guigsy's and Tony McCarroll's, with Liam Gallagher out front. Then Liam's older brother, a roadie for Inspiral Carpets, came to a gig and offered to take over, on the condition that he wrote everything.

years.h: Liam Gallagher replaces the singer in the Rain and renames it
years.p: [[Paul Arthurs|17aa0ede-a4bc-4a18-a347-0ee843a38d84]] invites [[Liam Gallagher|1f2345fa-344e-4863-a1d7-3958d57f4301]] in for Chris Hutton. Liam names the band after the Oasis Leisure Centre in Swindon, spotted on an Inspiral Carpets tour poster.

years.h: First gig at the Boardwalk, under the Catchmen and Sweet Jesus
years.p: Bottom of a three-band bill in Manchester. [[Noel Gallagher|6493ed80-8b44-49fa-91de-e7b0a0b57d6d]], working as a roadie for [[Inspiral Carpets|03c2e506-e8bb-4bd6-9693-5aa97c8eea1c]], is in the room.

years.cap: The Out of the Blue demo tape and its inlay, Manchester, autumn 1991
years.h: Noel joins, as sole songwriter and leader
years.p: That was the deal. Wikipedia's summary of what came next: a sound "so devoid of finesse and complexity that it came out sounding pretty much unstoppable."

years.cap: Oasis on stage at King Tut's Wah Wah Hut, Glasgow, May 31, 1993 (video still)
years.h: Oasis aren't on the bill at King Tut's. They play anyway
years.p: Sister Lovers' Debbie Ellis invited them to Glasgow. When the venue balked, the other bands threatened not to go on, and Oasis got four songs, ending with "I Am the Walrus."
years.xp:
[[Alan McGee|ffacc13a-01e5-4b5d-a455-6a7f302ac9ce]] of Creation Records was there by chance, to surprise Ellis, an old friend. "I looked over and saw Liam Gallagher for the first time. He looked amazing," he told Radio X. The Beatles cover settled it, and he offered a deal that night.

The set: "Rock 'n' Roll Star," "Bring It On Down," "Up in the Sky," "I Am the Walrus." A Japanese tourist, Ayako Misawa, filmed the first two songs on a Sony Handycam, the only known footage. McGee's and the band's accounts of how they got in still don't match.

years.h: Sony signs Oasis for the world, Creation gets Britain
years.p: An American deal was hard to land, so the band signed worldwide with Sony, which licensed them to Creation in the UK. A white-label "Columbia" went out to radio first.

eras.title: Fastest out of the gate
eras.text: Oasis's first full year on record took them from No. 31 to the fastest-selling debut album in British history at the time. It also included a deportation, a tambourine and Noel's first walkout.

years.h: Everyone but Noel is deported off a ferry to Amsterdam
years.p: A fight with other passengers on the crossing ends with four of the five sent home and the Amsterdam show cancelled.

years.h: "Supersonic" enters the chart at No. 31
years.p: The first single proper. The second, "Shakermaker," later cost the band $500,000 to the New Seekers over "I'd Like to Teach the World to Sing."
years.xp: A second claim came from Neil Innes, who sued over the likeness between the 1994 Christmas single "Whatever" and his song "How Sweet to Be an Idiot." Noel said in 2010 that it was unintentional and that he hadn't noticed until he was told.

years.h: Definitely Maybe goes straight in at No. 1
years.p: The fastest-selling debut album in Britain at the time. The cover was shot in Bonehead's house in Didsbury.
years.xp:
The first sessions, at Monnow Valley in Wales with Dave Batchelor, didn't work. The band re-cut it at Sawmills in Cornwall with Noel and Mark Coyle producing, and Owen Morris saved it in the mix, with Liam redoing vocals in London. It was mastered at Johnny Marr's studio in Manchester.

Michael Spencer Jones took the cover photo, with a nod to the Beatles' 1966 compilation and Egyptian art.

years.cap: Liam and Noel Gallagher on stage on the 1994 US tour
years.src: Wikipedia: Definitely Maybe Tour · Wikipedia: Oasis
years.h: A tambourine at the Whisky a Go Go sends Noel to Las Vegas
years.p: The band take meth with the Brian Jonestown Massacre before the Los Angeles show, thinking it's cocaine. Liam insults the crowd and hits Noel with a tambourine, and Noel flies out.
years.xp: Noel quit and went to San Francisco. Creation's Tim Abbot tracked him down in Las Vegas and talked him round. While he was gone he wrote "Talk Tonight" and "(It's Good) To Be Free," both recorded soon after in Austin, Texas.

eras.title: A quarter of a million a weekend
eras.text: In eighteen months Oasis changed drummers, lost a chart race to Blur, nearly lost a bassist, then played to more people in one weekend than any British band had outdoors. Two and a half million people tried to get in.

years.src: Wikipedia: Oasis · Wikipedia: Tony McCarroll · Wikipedia: Definitely Maybe Tour
years.h: "Some Might Say" goes to No. 1 and Tony McCarroll goes out
years.p: McCarroll's last show is Sheffield Arena on April 22. [[Alan White|03ee5b9c-6a28-4266-a773-83d6997ef4c4]], from Starclub, debuts on Top of the Pops playing the band's first No. 1.
years.xp:
Noel's explanation: "I like Tony as a geezer but he wouldn't have been able to drum the new songs." McCarroll said he had been "unlawfully expelled from the partnership" over a "personality clash" with the brothers.

He sued for £18 million in royalties and settled out of court in March 1999 for £550,000, giving up future royalties.

years.h: Blur and Oasis put out singles on the same Monday
years.p: [[Blur|ba853904-ae25-4ebb-89d6-c44cfbd71bd2]]'s "Country House" beats "Roll with It." Oasis's management blamed the price gap and Blur's extra B-sides; Creation blamed barcode problems.
years.xp: In The Observer, Noel said he hoped members of Blur would "catch AIDS and die." He later apologised in letters to the papers.

years.h: Guigsy leaves with nervous exhaustion. His stand-in lasts a few weeks
years.p: [[Paul McGuigan|e0a12f6d-1c89-467c-856a-e0d547c6c46f]] steps out and Scott McLeod of the Ya Ya's comes in, appearing on tour and in the "Wonderwall" video before quitting in the US.
years.xp: McLeod rang Noel to say he thought he'd made a mistake. Noel's reply: "I think you have, too. Good luck signing on." Bonehead covered on bass until McGuigan was talked back.

years.h: Morning Glory opens to mixed reviews and keeps selling
years.p: "Wonderwall," "Don't Look Back in Anger" and "Champagne Supernova," with [[Paul Weller|c4406045-e640-4cfe-8b88-4732cce314d4]] on guitar. By 2008 it was put at about 22 million copies, the UK's best-selling album of the 1990s.

years.h: The Gallaghers headline Maine Road, Manchester City's ground
years.p: The band's first headline outdoor shows are two nights at the home of the club the brothers had followed since they were kids.

years.cap: Noel Gallagher on the Knebworth stage, August 1996
years.h: Knebworth: 125,000 a night, and 2.5 million applied
years.p: Both nights sell out in minutes, a UK outdoor record. [[John Squire|a5fe0213-6f08-4369-8f16-5d15b329e56d]] of the Stone Roses joins for "Champagne Supernova" and "I Am the Walrus."
years.xp:
Two weeks earlier Oasis had played 80,000 people over two nights at Loch Lomond. The New York Times' Neil Strauss wrote that Oasis had unified "an entire country under the banner of a single pop act."

Jake Scott's 2021 film Oasis Knebworth 1996 was the highest-grossing documentary in the UK that year.

years.h: Liam skips MTV Unplugged and heckles Noel from the balcony
years.p: Citing a sore throat, Liam pulls out of the Royal Festival Hall taping. Noel sings, and Liam watches from a box with beer and cigarettes.

years.h: Liam spits beer across the MTV Video Music Awards stage
years.p: Mid-"Champagne Supernova" at Radio City, Liam gestures at Noel through his solo, spits beer and walks off. A few weeks later Noel flies home from the US tour on his own.

eras.title: Too much of everything
eras.text: Be Here Now was the fastest-selling album in British history at the time, and the man who wrote it later said it didn't stand up. Two years on, two founders were gone and Creation was running out of road.

years.src: Wikipedia: Be Here Now · Wikipedia: Oasis
years.h: Be Here Now sells 424,000 copies on its first day
years.p: Creation made journalists sign contracts not to discuss it, even with their partners. The cover puts a white Rolls-Royce in the swimming pool at Stocks House.
years.xp:
Owen Morris on the sessions: "Massive amounts of drugs. Big fights. Bad vibes." ITV's News at Ten covered the release, with Trevor McDonald saying "mad for it" on air.

Noel turned on it once he toured it. By 2003 it was "the sound of five men in the studio, on coke, not giving a fuck." Liam has called it his favourite Oasis record.

years.h: Fourteen B-sides become The Masterplan
years.p: Noel's own view: there was "a lot more inspired music on the B-sides than there is on Be Here Now itself."

years.h: Bonehead quits, Guigsy follows two weeks later
years.p: Bonehead's exit was billed as amicable. The brothers told a press conference: "The story and the glory will go on."
years.xp: Noel later told it differently: Wikipedia says Bonehead broke Noel's no drink or drugs rule during recording, and it ended in a confrontation.

years.h: Andy Bell from Ride takes the bass, which he'd never played
years.p: [[Gem Archer|7ac9c157-960e-43bb-880d-da1f13fcc5c4]] of Heavy Stereo comes in on guitar. After David Potts quits fast, [[Andy Bell|5946e805-9ab4-4fd9-9c19-21a8f7dfef98]], formerly of [[Ride|3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e]] and Hurricane #1, learns bass on the job.

eras.title: Big Brother, little brother
eras.text: With Creation folding, Oasis put their records out on their own label, Big Brother, and became a band where Liam and the new members wrote too. The brothers kept fighting, and in Paris in 2009 it finished.

years.h: Liam's first song arrives on Standing on the Shoulder of Giants
years.p: "Little James" is the first Oasis song Liam wrote. It's also the first record on Big Brother, the band's own label, set up as Creation folded.
play: Standing on the Shoulder of Giants

years.h: After a row with Liam in Barcelona, Noel quits overseas touring
years.p: Alan White's tendinitis forces a cancelled show. Noel and Liam fight, and Noel stops touring abroad, though he's back for the Wembley Stadium shows.

years.h: Liam's "Songbird" is the first Oasis single Noel didn't write
years.p: Heathen Chemistry goes to No. 1. Bell and Archer write too, and [[Johnny Marr|ff621094-2a76-401f-8398-b75b5fd2be24]] guests on guitar.

years.cap: Oasis on stage in Montreal, August 2002
years.h: Liam and Alan White are arrested after a Munich nightclub fight
years.p: Liam loses two front teeth; White is hit with an ashtray. Two years later Liam is fined about £40,000.

years.cap: Liam and Noel Gallagher in San Diego
years.h: Alan White is out, and Ringo's son is on the kit
years.p: White was fired on December 21, 2003. [[Zak Starkey|fa6d1fab-dc90-4e76-bdf9-28e06d1010ff]] drums but isn't made a member, so Oasis is a four-piece for the first time.

years.h: Dave Sardy produces, and critics call it the best since Morning Glory
years.p: Noel hands over the producer's chair after a decade. The tour runs to 113 shows in 26 countries, including Madison Square Garden and the Hollywood Bowl.

years.h: A stage invader in Toronto breaks three of Noel's ribs
years.p: At the Virgin Festival a man runs on and attacks Noel. Shows are cancelled while he recovers.

years.cap: Oasis at Slane Castle, Ireland, June 2009
q: I simply could not go on working with Liam a day longer.
years.h: Noel Gallagher quits Oasis backstage at Rock en Seine
years.p: A fight in Paris, two dates from the end of the tour. Bloc Party's Kele Okereke tells the crowd Oasis won't be playing; two hours later Noel says he has quit.
years.xp:
Days earlier a Chelmsford show had been cancelled. Noel later blamed Liam's "hangover"; Liam sued, saying a doctor had diagnosed laryngitis, and dropped it after Noel apologised.

Noel in 2015: with six months off he'd have "just forgotten about it," but "the straw that broke the camel's back was the night in Paris and that was a fight."

eras.title: Two bands, one surname
eras.text: Liam kept the rest of the band and called it Beady Eye; Noel started the High Flying Birds.

years.h: Liam thanks everyone at the Brits except Noel
years.p: Morning Glory wins Best British Album of the Last 30 Years. Liam collects it alone, thanks Bonehead, Guigsy and White, then throws his mic and the award into the crowd.

years.h: Beady Eye and Noel Gallagher's High Flying Birds
years.p: Liam, Archer and Bell make two albums as [[Beady Eye|a0e10984-0eca-4920-a171-5fd7a62ee069]] before splitting in 2014. Noel's band makes four. Bell goes back to [[Ride|3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e]].

eras.title: The guns fall silent
eras.text: Liam spent his Definitely Maybe anniversary tour leaving an empty seat for Noel at every show. A month later, the brothers announced they were back.

years.cap: Liam and Noel Gallagher in the 2024 reunion photo
years.h: "The great wait is over": Oasis announce a 2025 tour
years.p: The announcement photos show only the brothers. Bonehead, Archer and Bell are revealed later. Definitely Maybe, reissued for its 30th, goes back to No. 1.
years.xp:
The full statement: "The guns have fallen silent. The stars have aligned. The great wait is over. Come see. It will not be televised."

A week after the reissue, Time Flies and Morning Glory were at Nos. 3 and 4 and "Live Forever" charted higher than it had in 1994.

years.cap: Oasis at the Principality Stadium, Cardiff, July 4, 2025
years.h: In Cardiff the brothers share a stage for the first time since 2009
years.p: The tour opens at the Principality Stadium with "Hello." Liam asks whether it was worth "the £40,000 you paid for the ticket."
years.xp:
Noel introduced Joey Waronker as their "14th drummer" and dedicated "The Masterplan" to fans in their 20s who'd never seen the band. Cast and [[Richard Ashcroft|2d1d8985-47bc-4244-8cc3-577584e411f6]] opened.

A fan died after a fall from the upper tier at Wembley on August 2; the band said they were shocked and saddened. In October Bonehead stepped away from the Asian and Australian legs after a prostate cancer diagnosis, which he announced himself. The tour ended in São Paulo on November 23, with a tribute to Mani.

years.h: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducts all eight, McCarroll too
years.p: The Gallaghers, Arthurs, McGuigan, McCarroll, White, Archer and Bell are named. The ceremony is set for November 14 in Los Angeles, and both brothers say they'll be there.

years.h: Oasis Live '27: 38 dates, no new songs
years.p: The world tour takes in the UK, Ireland, Europe and the US. Noel tells talkSPORT there won't be new material.
